The '''1961–62 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|59th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|30th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. 

The season saw Real Madrid win the [[Double (association football)#Spain|domestic double]] and get agonizingly close to clinching its first ever [[Treble (association football)|treble]] (similarly to the [[1957–58 Real Madrid CF season|1957–58 season]]), only to be defeated by [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in an exhilarating [[1962 European Cup Final|European Cup final]]. 

By successfully defending the league championship, Madrid secured their 8th Primera División title and equaled Barcelona for most title wins. 

==Summary==
The club won its eight title ever, second in a row. Head coach Miguel Muñoz started the renewal of the squad with Araquistáin as goalkeeper, Pachín reinforcing the defensive line playing along Santamaría,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/realmadrid-in-ec.html|title=Real Madrid CF – All the players in European Cups|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|accessdate=24 February 2015}}</ref> Miera, Isidro, and Pedro Casado. The midfield was covered by Luis Del Sol and Felix Ruiz. Meanwhile, ageing forwards Di Stefano and Puskas were aimed with passes by Gento and Justo Tejada.<ref>{{cite web|work=Mundo Deportivo|title=Galería de internacionales: Justo Tejada Martinez|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1989/01/03/pagina-29/1187520/pdf.html#|page=29|language=Spanish|date=3 January 1989}}</ref>

Also, the club won the [[1962 Copa del Generalísimo Final]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mexico.as.com/mexico/2017/06/03/futbol/1496525382_712263.html|title=Doblete del Real Madrid|publisher=as.com}}</ref> defeating Sevilla 2–1 and clinching the club's first [[Double (association football)#Spain|domestic double]]. It was the only [[Copa del Generalísimo]] that [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] won in 11 campaigns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/04/19/futbol/copa_rey/1303215006.html|title=La única Copa de Di Stefano|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=Spanish}}</ref> The squad reached the [[1962 European Cup Final]], where it was defeated by Portuguese side and European incumbents [[Benfica]] 3–5 (with all Madrid's goals scored by Puskás) thanks to a superb second half, with star forward [[Eusébio]] scoring 2 goals.<ref name = "trivela">{{cite web|url=http://trivela.uol.com.br/eusebio-ainda-e-sim-maior-que-cristiano-ronaldo/|title=Eusébio ainda é, sim, maior que Cristiano Ronaldo|author=LEAL, Ubiratan|date=6 January 2014|publisher=Trivela|access-date=7 January 2020|language=Portuguese|archive-date=13 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170713113747/http://trivela.uol.com.br/eusebio-ainda-e-sim-maior-que-cristiano-ronaldo/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Had Madrid won the European Cup in May, its subsequent triumph in the Copa del Generalísimo would have secured the club its first ever [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]], something no club had achieved at the time. As of 2022, Real Madrid still has not won a treble.
